title: Austria Hungary's Navy Was a Complete Disaster in WW1 Here's Why
fullText: in June 1918 one of the most modern battleships in Europe was sunk by a wooden boat small enough to fit in your driveway and remarkably  that was not even the most embarrassing thing  to happen to the Austro Hungarian Navy that year this was a fleet that spent almost the entire war hiding in port whose four modern dreadnoughts fired their main guns at an enemy warship exactly zero times and whose flagship went to the bottom flying somebody else's flag and yet it was built at enormous expense champion personally by the heir to the throne and was in some respects  ahead of the British and the French its most successful submarine captain by the way  was the guy from The Sound of music but we'll get to him so  this raises the obvious question why did the Austro Hungarian navy perform so miserably in the First World War now you'd think that a mostly landlocked empire built on Central European farmland wouldn't care much about battleships and for most of its history you'd be right Austria Hungary kept a small navy which patrolled the Adriatic and bothered nobody in particular  but between 1904  and 1914 that changed and the coastal patrol force turned into a proper blue water navy with four brand new dreadnoughts and the reason for this sudden and very expensive upgrade was mostly  one man that man  was Archduke Franz Ferdinand Ferdinand had been obsessed with the navy since serving in it as a young officer he held the honorary rank of admiral personally launched two of the four dreadnoughts and burned through his political capital forcing naval budgets past a parliament which did not want to pay for any of it without Ferdinand the empire probably never builds a real navy at all which brings us to a bit of a problem because  on June 28th, 1914 Ferdinand was shot dead in Sarajevo meaning  that at the exact moment Austria Hungary declared the very war this navy had been built to fight the navy lost the only friend  it had  in high places his body by the way was shipped home aboard the very first Dreadnought he'd fought to fund  which is the kind of symbolism you really don't want at the start of a war so the war began and the fleet's commander Admiral House did some maths his four dreadnoughts were the only serious weight the Empire had at sea if he lost them the Adriatic was gone if he kept them in harbour their mere existence would pin down the entire French and Italian fleets also the allies had strung a barrier of ships and nets across the Strait of Otranto to keep the Austrians in over the entire war this barrier caught a grand total of two submarines but it looked very intimidating on a map and for the admirals that was enough so the fleet stayed in port  for years now you might be wondering how Austria Hungary paid for four dreadnoughts at all given that Hungary famously hated funding the military the answer was a deal Hungary would approve the naval budget but only if the fourth Dreadnought the Cent Ishtvan was built in a Hungarian shipyard which sounded like a reasonable compromise right up until someone checked and discovered that Hungary didn't own a shipyard capable of building a Dreadnought the chosen yard had spent its life building merchant ships and had to be enlarged and reequipped before work could even begin as a result Saint Ishtvan took three years longer than her sisters cost more and was held together by riveting so bad that naval historians still wince at it this will become relevant meanwhile  the fleet sat  and sat by early 1918 the sailors had been stuck in harbour for over three years and thanks to the Allied blockade their rations had been cut twice coffee sugar and meat had essentially stopped existing for the enlisted men that is the officers were still eating rather well which the enlisted men could both see and smell and then news arrived that sailors in Russia had recently solved a similar problem by overthrowing their entire government on February 1st, 1918 crews at the naval base of Cataro raised the red flag and within two hours around 40 ships had joined them their demands boiled down to bread and peace which was awkward because the empire was out of both loyal ships turned up within three days the mutiny collapsed and four ringleaders were shot the fleet commander was quietly retired and replaced by a certain Meeklosh Horty who had diagnosed the navy's core problem as not attacking anyone and intended to fix it in June 1918 Horthy decided to finally use the dreadnoughts for their actual job smashing the Otranto barrier so that the submarines could get out into the Mediterranean and so on the night of June 9th Saint Istvan and her sister tzigethoff steamed out of Pola for the first meaningful operation of their careers which at around 3:15 the next morning ran into an Italian named Luigi Rizzo Rizzo commanded a m s boat 12 meters long made of wood armed with two torpedoes he slipped between the escorting destroyers close to 300 meters and put both torpedoes into Szent Isztvan two boiler rooms flooded the famous Hungarian riveting gave up and she rolled over and sank in under three hours the whole thing was filmed from her sister ship which is why the only footage of a battleship sinking in the First World War is of this one 89 men died and here's the kicker cent  istván  is Hungarian for Saint Stephen the patron saint of Hungary so the ship named to honour Hungary was sunk on her first ever sortie by Hungarian workmanship in a war that Hungary had never wanted to pay for Horthy called off the operation and the surface fleet never left port again by late October 1918 the empire was visibly falling apart rather than hand his fleet to the allies Emperor Carl gave the entire navy to the newly declared state of Slovenes Croats and Serbs which at that point had been a country for about two days on the evening of October the imperial flag came down on the flagship Viribus Unitis and a Croatian officer Yanko Vukovich took command of the fleet a command he would hold for roughly 14 hours because unfortunately for him two Italians had spent that same night riding a modified torpedo into the harbour and attaching a mine to the flagship's hull they were fished out of the water shortly afterwards and helpfully told everyone what they'd just done so Vukovich evacuated the ship but when the mine failed to explode on schedule he concluded he'd been pranked and climbed back aboard the mine went off  14 minutes later Bukovec went down with a flagship he commanded for half a day sunk by an attack aimed at a navy which technically no longer existed the Italians upon finding out sent their prize money to his widow which was polite if a little late meanwhile down at Kataro the officer hauling down the Imperial Naval flag for the last time was the Empire's most successful submarine captain Georg von trap yes that guyog von trap  before the singing the curtains and the escape over the Alps he sank more Allied ships than any other Habsburg commander history is strange like that and that was the end of the Austro Hungarian navy of its four dreadnoughts two were sunk one was handed to Italy for scrap and one was given to France which used her for target practice making that fittingly the most action she ever saw all in all a fleet that spent so much of the war doing nothing that its own sailors mutinied out of hunger and boredom a position from which it would never really recover
